verdicts.reason: Descriptive overview of PCPI purpose; nothing to verify or exercise.
Quote states the core asserts pcpi_valid and drives pcpi_insn, pcpi_rs1, pcpi_rs2 on an unsupported instruction with PCPI enabled. Observable at the interface.
Quote says an external core can decode, execute and assert pcpi_ready. It is optional behaviour of the slave, exercised by a scenario.
Quote says a result can optionally be written to pcpi_rd with pcpi_wr asserted. Optional slave behaviour, exercised by a scenario.
Quote states the core decodes rd and writes pcpi_rd to that register. This needs register-file visibility, so a scenario is the right check.
Quote states an illegal instruction exception is raised and the handler is called when no PCPI core acknowledges within 16 cycles. Tested with a scenario.

Quote says a slow PCPI core should assert pcpi_wait once decoded and keep it asserted until pcpi_ready. 'More than a couple of cycles' is vague, but the pcpi_wait/pcpi_ready relation is checkable from interface signals.
Quote states that pcpi_wait prevents the core from raising an illegal instruction exception. Tested by a scenario.

questions.question: Is the 16-cycle timeout counted from pcpi_valid assertion? Does asserting pcpi_wait suspend the timeout indefinitely, or only until pcpi_ready? What happens if pcpi_wait is asserted after cycle 16?
What does 'more than a couple of cycles' mean in cycles? When must pcpi_wait be asserted so that it counts as being asserted 'as soon as' the instruction is decoded?
Must pcpi_wr be asserted in the same cycle as pcpi_ready, or can it be asserted earlier? Is pcpi_rd sampled only when pcpi_ready is high?
